note: Adds 'I do not seek anything' before 'except'; source has only 'except'.
Hebrew 'they commanded Joseph' rendered as 'they sent to Joseph'; the commanding idea is lost.
'Saying' is rendered as passive 'it was said to them,' changing the speaker.
Changes subject: source says the locust will not be able to see the land; Arabic says 'no one can see the land'.
Adds 'he showed his greatness' not in the source, which states only that they dealt arrogantly.
Adds 'unjustly' (ظلماً), a qualifier not in the source's absolute prohibition.
Hebrew has 'and he is found in his hand' (conjunction); Arabic renders it 'or is found', changing the condition to an alternative.
Adds that the owner accepts the oath; source says the owner shall take the animal, and adds 'the keeper' as subject.
Pronoun shift: 'its sound' (the robe's) instead of 'his voice' (Aaron's).
Renders 'in his baldness or in his forehead' as 'in the back of the garment or its front'—wrong idea, omits baldness/forehead.
Adds clause 'and its blood is bound to its life' not in the source.
Adds 'even for a moment' (ولو لحظة) not in source; omits the idea of the holy thing 'being swallowed' (כבלע).
Adds 'the others' as subject of setting up the tabernacle; source does not specify who set it up.
Adds 'qataif' pastry; source compares taste to fresh oil, not oil cakes.

Renders 'I will not turn it back' as 'I cannot turn back his blessing,' adding inability.
'prostrate at your feet' rendered 'sit at your feet'; singular 'he accepts/bears from your words' made plural 'they carry'

Adds 'no longer/again' (لم يعودوا) not in source's 'they did not say'.
Adds 'he left them' (أبقاهم), which is not in the source.

'their root is in Amalek' changed to 'their root came from Amalek' (adds 'came', changes 'in' to 'from')
Adds 'willingly' and object 'it to him' not in the source's 'we will surely give'.

Statement 'I will die of thirst' turned into a rhetorical question ('shall I die...?').
Adds 'recompense' and 'to her'; changes 'when they come' to 'let us go'.
Adds 'the two previous times'; source says only 'as at other times/as before'.
Reverses final clause to 'you are not guilty'; also renders 'grant them to us' as 'be gentle with them'.
Reverses meaning: source says death WILL separate me and you; Arabic says 'if anything other than death separates'.
'Razor' (מוֹרָה) is mistranslated as 'Moses' (موسى), so the razor not touching his head is lost.
Adds 'the third band' where source says 'one band'.

Renders 'what he says' as 'what happens', changing the idea.

Hebrew is a statement ('I will take... and give'), Arabic turns it into a rhetorical question ('Shall I take...?').
Omits the place name Nachon ('to Nachon'); says only that Saul had indeed arrived.

Renders 'the people will see me' as 'the people frightened me' (different idea)
Changes 'we are like ten thousand' to 'you equal ten thousand of us' — subject/person shifted from we to you.
Arabic says 'my way' where source has 'his way'.
Renders singular 'your servant' as plural 'your servants' (عبيدك).
Arabic adds causal 'because she lay upon him' instead of 'the night on which she lay upon him'.
'Of Solomon's reign' attached to 'second month' instead of 'fourth year'; fourth year of reign not stated

Omits 'and he spoke to him' (אָמַר לוֹ) between giving bread and giving land.
Adds 'of Baal' to 'all the prophets', a specification not in the source.

Adds 'the house of the LORD' as object of building, not in source.
Person change: 'we ate and were satisfied' instead of 'the people ate and were satisfied'.
Adds 'from' as sender and omits 'then' at the start.
Renders 'and so forth' as 'and at that time', adding a temporal idea not in the source.
Adds 'translated' (مترجمة), which is not in the source's 'plainly read'.
Adds 'with him,' which is not in the source.
Last clause says the people of Jerusalem left the city to the Broad Wall, instead of they fortified/restored Jerusalem as far as the wall.
Adds that the fields and vineyards are pledged; the source only names them.
Adds 'part of' to the hundred of silver, changing the amount; also omits the entreaty 'we pray'.
Adds the vocative 'O God' not present in the source.
Arabic changes plural 'them/they' to dual 'them two/they two', adding a dual referent not in source.
Adds 'the guards' as subject and uses dual 'to them' instead of plural.
Adds 'dwelling' and renders 'in Judah and in Benjamin' as 'from Judah in Benjamin'.
Adds 'wheat' to 'heaps'; source says only heaps.
Source has the night personified as speaker ('the night that said'); Arabic renders it passively 'in which it was said,' changing the speaker.

Changes 'your fear is your confidence' to 'your reliance is on your fear' and links hope to integrity of ways.
Adds 'how much more' (فكم بالحري); source says 'even'.

Turns 'I am blameless' into a conditional 'if I were perfect'.
Arabic makes 'I am wicked' conditional ('if I am guilty'), changing assertion to hypothesis.
Changes the statement 'to dust you will return me' into a question.
Renders 'host with me' as 'host against me' and adds 'circumstances change'.

Arabic says 'who does not know such things' instead of 'who does not have such things'.
Renders 'until he fulfills his day' as 'until he is happy in his day,' changing the predicate's meaning.
Statements turned into rhetorical questions ('Does the wise answer...? Does he fill...?')
Question word changed from 'what' to 'why' in both clauses.
'Moving of my lips will restrain' changed to 'consolation of my lips will lighten from you'—adds consolation/lighten, omits moving/restrain.

Renders 'you shall treat me as a stranger' as 'be arrogant against me', changing the idea.

Adds 'floods' as agent not in source; source says his increase shall be carried/flow away.
Statement 'They are like stubble' turned into a question 'Will they be...?'
Negation reversed: 'our substance is not cut down' becomes affirmative 'our resisters have perished'.
Calls the Almighty 'your gold' instead of 'your defense'; adds gold and omits defense.
"he would put [strength] in me" rendered as "he listens to me" — different idea.
"until the end of light with darkness" changed to "a boundary between light and darkness" — idea altered.

Arabic changes plural 'they clap their hands' to feminine singular 'she claps with her hands'.
Arabic says 'claim of one I did not know' instead of 'controversy I did not know'; adds a person and shifts the object.
Adds 'forsaken' and 'their place was' not in the source; the wilderness-desolation image is recast.
Changes 'Who will give of his flesh? We are not satisfied' into 'who finds one not satisfied with his flesh'.
Adds 'always' (دائمًا) to elders understanding judgment.
Source says 'all his words'; Arabic says 'all his actions/deeds'.
Changes 'by their instruction he seals' to 'he seals their instruction,' omitting the means idea.

Adds 'more' and changes 'from my sin' to 'more than my sin.'
Adds 'effeminate' (الْمُخَنَّثِينَ) not present in the source's 'consecrated.'

Statement ('He shut the sea') changed into a question ('Who shut...?').

Adds 'land' as object and 'vegetation' not present in source.

Adds 'my words' (كلامي) as object of despising, not present in the source.

Renders 'will submit to me' as 'flatter me,' changing the predicate/idea.

Omits 'from afar' (מרחוק); only 'from ancient times' is kept.
